newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Christmas mixed bag for British stores.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Christmas mixed bag for British stores.

text.p: Four British retailers gave their verdict on Christmas on Wednesday, showing that trading was reasonable but far from the spending binge some had hoped for.
Strong demand for big ticket household items, which has favoured more upmarket shops, clearly helped department store chain Allders Plc.
But cosmetics chain Body Shop International Plc found trading in Britain was below expectations, with like-for-like sales down two percent in the 10 weeks over Christmas and New Year.

Clothing and textiles group Laura Ashley Holdings Plc saw like-for-like sales at its stores in Britain rise 10 percent in the six weeks from November 24 to January 4. But the overall performance was held back by an eight percent drop in same-store sales in continental Europe.
Kingfisher Plc, whose outlets include Woolworths, electricals chain Comet and B&Q, said its like-for-like sales rose 7.8 percent in the nine weeks to January 4.

The mixed performance was mirrored in the companies' share prices, with Kingfisher down 11 pence at 659, Allders up 11-1/2 at 171-1/2, Body Shop down six at 189-1/2 and Laura Ashley down 1-1/2 at 156-1/2.

Allders saw comparable sales rise 11.6 percent in the first 15 weeks of its financial year, which the group said would translate into substantially higher trading profits than the same period a year ago.
Chief executive Harvey Lipsith said: "The very encouraging sales growth reported recently has continued through Christmas and the start of the winter sale, our most important trading period."
Overall sales grew 37.4 percent and like-for-like sales in the latest three weeks, the beginning of the store's winter sale, were up 15.9 percent.
Body Shop's sales on a like-for-like basis in the 10 weeks to January 4 were down two percent overall. They fell two percent in the United States, four percent in Europe and four percent in Asia.
Chairman Gordon Roddick said: "Our Christmas trading has been mixed...In Europe, the sales performance was varied with the UK coming in below expectations."

He said the fall in comparable store sales in Asia reflected "generally softer seasonal trading in a number of territories." But he said total sales growth continued to be fuelled by expansion in those markets.

Laura Ashley said the sales breakdown for the 23 weeks from the end of July to January 4 showed a clear dip in North American sales last autumn on both a total and like-for-like basis, but this reflected the closure of 19 shops. A recovery fed through over Christmas when the region's like-for-like sales rose by 1.0 percent.
"The new shops, another 12 of which opened in the fourth quarter, are beginning to show top line growth and contributed to the improved performance in the six week christmas period."
Chief executive Ann Iverson, brought in to revitalise the firm, said she was pleased with the performance.
"We remain fully on track for this financial year and for 1007/98," she said in a statement.

Kingfisher's Woolworths store sales were 8.1 percent on a like-for-like basis, helped by strong sales of toys and home essentials. At Comet, like-for-like sales were up 14 percent and home improvement chain B&Q saw sales rise 10.5 percent on a like-for-like basis.

Drugs and personal care chain Superdrug had a five percent increase in like-for-like sales. At Darty, Kingfisher's French electrical retailer, sales in local currency terms were up 4.7 percent after adjusting for 8.0 million pounds of sales from New Vanden Borre. Like-for-like sales were up 2.4 percent. ($1=.5979 Pound)
